headings.title: System flow map and sequence index

html:
System flow map and sequence index

Use this map to follow a request across the system and find the owner of each transition. The architecture overview introduces the components; this page connects their internal flows to detailed guides and source folders. An arrow means a transfer of input, state or evidence. It does not mean that all connected writes are one transaction or that the caller has received a disk-save acknowledgement.

For declared branch execution, human checkpoints and graph recovery, see Activity dependencies.

The execution path

flowchart TD User[User input and explicit controls] --> Admission[API and task admission] Event[Schedules, monitors and workflow invocations] --> Tasks[Durable task owner] Admission --> Tasks Admission --> Direct[Direct request preparation] Tasks --> Dispatch[Accepted attempt dispatch] Direct --> Dispatch Config[Accepted settings, parameters and target identity] --> Dispatch Dispatch --> Host[RuntimeHost] Host --> Loop[Owned AgentLoop] Loop --> Context[Bounded model context and advertised tools] Context --> Model[Configured model endpoint] Model --> Decision[Complete response validation and acceptance fence] Decision --> Control[Native controls: discovery, waits, completion] Decision --> Activities[Activity or direct invocation owner] Activities --> Engine[ExecutionEngine and registered adapter] Authority[Current permission, target and resource authority] --> Engine Engine --> Local[Controller-local service or isolated worker] Engine --> Gateway[Selected Gateway service] Local --> Result[Actual result and operation receipt] Gateway --> Result Result --> Loop Control --> Loop Loop --> Publication[Accepted run and response publication] Publication --> View[Trace, conversation and artifact views] View --> User

The Controller is the decision owner; the model proposes decisions, and the selected adapter performs the operation. Most ordinary external capability calls enter Activity admission even when there is only one call. Interactive controls can use the direct path. An operation claim, its actual result and a published answer are separate facts. Neither partial provider output nor browser progress authorizes an external effect.

Follow this transition Detailed owner and implementation

Separate task, model, Activity and resource admission Scheduling and concurrency.
Reserve a model decision, wait for endpoint capacity and accept or discard its response Model decisions, capacity and cancellation.
Suspend for a job, event, input or authorization Jobs and waits, reply sequence, Full Access, checks and authority.
Interpret the task and validate completion Task Contract Compiler, completion normalization.

Inspect process health, heartbeat freshness, local GPU history or Python stacks Diagnostic console flows.

State and information flow

The native journal and receipts retain execution evidence. Context is a bounded projection supplied to a model, while conversation history is a presentation of retained turns. Neither is a replacement for the native operation owner. A Controller checkpoint and a Gateway checkpoint belong to different state owners.

flowchart TD Input[Prompt, attachments and accepted parameter references] --> Run[Native run and task records] Result[Operation results and receipts] --> Run Run --> Context[Model context projection] Notes[Task Context, Agent KV and Memory] --> Context Context --> Model[Model request] Run --> Trace[Trace and activity projection] Trace --> Chat[Retained conversation turns and search indexes] Result --> Artifacts[Artifact identity, versions and files] Artifacts --> Views[Preview, download and response publication] Chat --> Views Run --> Hub[Controller RAM repositories] Notes --> Hub Chat --> Hub Hub --> Save[Committed Controller recovery generation] Target[Gateway jobs and physical operation evidence] --> GHub[Gateway RAM state] GHub --> GSave[Gateway recovery checkpoint] Target --> Result

The diagram groups ownership rather than showing every storage adapter. Artifact bytes and retained output have their own payload lifecycles; a metadata row alone does not imply that its file is available. Derived search/index state can be rebuilt from retained records. RAM acceptance and disk persistence remain separate.

Information or lifecycle Authoritative guide

Context IDs, attachment access, read budgets and exact data Artifacts and context, context and memory, attachments and Vision.
Task-local scratch ownership, explicit reads/writes and permanent deletion fences Agent KV sequences.
Parameters, frozen accepted values and exact invocation bindings Parameter storage and bindings, recorded reviews, atomic approvals and future mapped calls.
Pause to correct a call, recover Apply or teach and launch an ordered sequence Correction sessions and learned-workflow flows.
Composer metadata search, resource selection, attachment grants and stale responses Composer resource flows.
Retain prompt text, group similar prompts and insert history completion Prompt recall flows.
Artifacts, collection, versions, publication and downloads Artifacts and output.
Activity, timing, command output and model-output inspection Observability, trace subscription sequence.
Optional consumer redaction and unchanged canonical literals Redaction.
Conversation navigation, durable deletion intent and asynchronous cleanup Conversation lifecycle.
Gateway jobs, transfers, local checkpoints and unknown physical outcomes Gateway state; state publication and recovery sequences.
Notification production, delivery, inbox state and observation Notifications.

Capability families and their boundaries

skills/catalog.py explicitly composes the bundled factories below. Registration is not selection or permission. A run's accepted capability ceiling, selected surface, current authority and target availability still determine what can execute. The generated Tool and Skill Reference lists the registered tool contracts; individual source-folder guides explain their adapters.

flowchart TD Bundled[Bundled skill factories] --> Registry[CapabilityRegistry] External[Registered user Python skills] --> Registry Optional[Inference skill when build feature is enabled] --> Registry Registry --> Ceiling[Accepted capability ceiling and selection] Ceiling --> Catalog[Run catalog and advertised schemas] Catalog --> Proposal[Validated model proposal] Proposal --> Checks[Dispatch, schema, permission and target checks] Checks --> Adapter[Registered deterministic executor] Adapter --> Controller[Controller service or isolated worker] Adapter --> Gateway[Selected Gateway] Controller --> Evidence[Result or explicit failure] Gateway --> Evidence

These groups are a navigation aid; they do not imply that every tool in a group uses the same process or transport.

Family Source folders and detailed flow guides
Runtime and configuration Settings, Conversation, Task, Agent, System, Gateway, Docs.
Task knowledge and values Task Context, KV, Memory, Parameters, Database; see context and memory.
Scheduled and repeatable work Recipe, Schedule, Monitor, Notification; see tasks, events, Workflows, monitor execution flows.
Execution, files and artifacts Shell, Python, File, Artifact, Docker; see native Files, command Working Context.
Documents and visual output Office, PDF, Visualization, Vision; see Office, PDF, attachments and Vision.
Desktop and target observation Desktop, Clipboard, Screen, UI, Browser; see desktop, clipboard, screen, browser, UI automation.
Host infrastructure GPU, Local AI, Proxmox; see GPU, Gateway Local AI, Proxmox.
Web access and research HTTP, Web, Web Research; see HTTP, Web Research.
Identity and generic mail Auth, Email; see authentication and email.
Provider integrations Gmail, Google Calendar, Google Drive, Microsoft 365, GitHub, Slack; see Gmail boundary and the corresponding user guides.

Working Context also composes git, ssh, kubernetes, slurm, database, http and proxmox adapters. Those adapters retain setup/resource facts; their registration in working_context_adapters() does not create additional skills. New bundled skills follow skill authoring. Independently authored Python skills use the user-skill worker and SDK.

Supporting systems

These packages participate in startup, hosting, model availability or distribution; they are not additional Agent decision loops.

System Lifecycle and source owners
Server bootstrap, login, readiness and shutdown Server lifecycle; smto_runtime, application composition.
Linux, macOS and Windows Gateways Gateway architecture and sequences; gateway_core, Linux, macOS, Windows.
Main/Helper/Vision model routes and optional inference management Model configuration, inference management, Controller lifecycle and binding sequences, status and telemetry flows, Portal launch and worker cleanup, shared inference architecture; controller_inference, inference_portal.
External model launch profiles llama.cpp, Ollama, vLLM; these scripts have hardware/model prerequisites and are separate from ordinary request execution.
Desktop/mobile presentation, commands and product identity UI ownership, command palette, branding compatibility.
Prompt selection and compact guidance Compact guidance, prompt editor, prompt sources.
Errors, canonical legal material and manual delivery Diagnostics, error_catalog, smto_legal, manual service.
Packaging, installers, public site and release assets Build tooling, packaging, public site.
Verify compiled setup inputs, serialize dependency work and repair one private directory Compiled setup primitives and scoped repair.

Track installation resources, stop owned processes and remove recorded files Installation state and bounded removal.
Source navigation and documentation checks Source map, documentation architecture, architecture folder inventory.

For a concrete operation, follow its detailed guide into the linked implementation and tests. A rendered diagram establishes readable structure; the operation's transaction, authorization and failure contracts remain with those owners.
